required_change: §4.11 *The clock* (4): after '… that no other epoch falls on (DR28: a destructive event is epoch content; V08 §3.6 (3); J-V8.55)' add '— a newly carried calamity dated at or before the last epoch's week folds no epoch at its own week: it rides the first epoch the absorb folds (with none, the port folds one at the absorb's week for it), its `EpochInputs.events` entry at that epoch's first week (the last epoch's week + 1), its own tick kept in its receipt, so its hazard strikes and its deaths reach the burial need; with the absorb's week itself before the last epoch's (V08 §3.6's degenerate row) it folds no epoch and its dated changes apply finished, noted'. claim: CATALOGUE-GAP (raised ways x part-0 ways laid after them; the catalogue pairs raised with edit and epoch only by keyword). Once a raised way stands, a part-0 way laid across its under-deck strip has no rule keeping it off the piers or out of a `vault` span. §2.7's support step (3) slides piers off 'a part-0 way's corridor' (base l.2528-2529) and the span rule opens a span over a way (l.2575-2577) only for the ways standing when they run, and nothing re-runs them for a later way: only (6) for a trace or moat and §4.11's carve for a channel (l.8128). The later ways carry no support obstacle: §4.3's lattice costs (l.5559-5563: water, reservation, wall, existing fabric, land value, the class grade limit) name none; S5c's legality (l.5855-5860: spines, shores, wall setback bands, reservations, the stage boundary, walls, water) none; §7.1's ground `drawWay` (l.10295-10297) and E-07 have no bend or refusal for a pier (V09's `bend.raised.*` keys cover raised strokes only). V06 runs `raisedWays` (step 10a) before `growth` (step 14; V06 l.1004, l.1008), and the growth's S5-S13 on new faces re-runs no support step. Only a raised course (V06 §3.19 (5), l.2797), a new trace (V06 §3.7.6 (5), l.1581-1582), stage 2's own laying (V01 §3.17.3 (3), l.2469-2477: 'never along the strip, never through a pier') and S8's holes (§4.6 l.6375-6379) keep off the piers. So an epoch growing a stage over a standing aqueduct's or viaduct's land (H-AQUA's case), an epoch route re-solve, or a hand road drawn across a viaduct lays a street over pier rings or through an arch-vault chamber. Masonry piers stand every 8-15 m, each 0.2 of its span wide (V11 l.3949), so most such crossings meet one. Nothing catches it: §5.3 holds no support invariant, T110-2's 'zero junctions' passes, and S8's holes keep only plots out. A street through a masonry pier is an impossible result on a CITY epoch's common path, the same class as 'a support standing in water'.

Its under-deck strip is crossed only under an `open` span whose clear width holds the way's corridor + `raisedWays.structure.clearWidthM` and whose soffit meets §2.7's clearance for the crossed class, within ± `raisedWays.structure.squareDeg` of square to the deck. The route's crossing shifts along the strip to the nearest such span, else the route takes another course by F-ROUTE's ladder.' §4.4 S5c's legality adds: 'a proposal meeting a standing raised way's strip anywhere else is deflected along it to the nearest such span, or ends at the strip as at a reservation.' This is the one rule V01 §3.17.3 (3) states for stage 2. Its two cells move to V11 §3.24.2's `raisedWays.structure` (`clearWidthM` 1 m, `squareDeg` 30°), and V01 §3.17.3 (3) cites §4.3 (principle (9): one mechanism; equivalence: V01's crossing rule, ladder and values unchanged). Ends (R3-01): determinism §7.1, a ground `drawWay` or a moved way crossing a standing raised way's strip elsewhere is bent at its dry run to the nearest such span (E-07's row; V09 §4.9 `bend.raised.underSpan`); V06 §3.6 and §3.19 cite §4.3 for the growth and route re-solves; scope §13.2 T110-2 adds 'an H-AQUA epoch growing a stage over a standing aqueduct's land, an epoch route re-solved under a viaduct, and a hand road drawn across one: 0 way corridors over a support ring or a `vault` span, every crossing under an `open` span'. At generation, VEW-r3-02's re-run slides the piers off the ways S5b and S5c grew.
